title: A range whose iterator() makes a fresh iterator

blocks.text: `Collection.iterator()` is the page's JDK example of a factory method: every collection returns **its own** `Iterator`, and the client only sees the interface. Each call makes **a new iterator**, which is why two loops over one list never disturb each other.
Write `Range implements Iterable<Integer>` for the integers from `start` (inclusive) to `end` (exclusive). `iterator()` is your factory method.

items: Each `iterator()` call returns a new, independent iterator.
`new Range(a, b)` with `b < a` is refused with `IllegalArgumentException`.

cases.says: A for-each loop over new Range(3, 7) sees 3, 4, 5, 6.
Two iterators from one range each start at the beginning, and advancing one does not move the other.
next() after the last element throws NoSuchElementException.
new Range(5, 5) yields nothing: hasNext() is false at once.

concepts: Collection.iterator() is a JDK factory method: each collection returns its own Iterator, a new one per call, and clients see only the interface.
